answer: Sybil Anchoring: Each agent must commit a resource akin to a pearl—unique and valuable—to establish identity. The system enforces hollow verification, requiring periodic replenishment of this resource at increasing intervals. Attackers face escalating costs as multiples must sustain jetty-like infrastructure, scaling nonlinearly with each new identity. The per-identity cost grows with time and volume, making mass impersonation prohibitively expensive.
